concept: Hook additional-context injection into the first message
summary: additionalContext is wrapped in a system reminder and inserted into the conversation where the hook fired; it never shows as a chat message.

facts.text: additionalContext is wrapped in a system reminder and inserted into the conversation where the hook fired; it never shows as a chat message.
Plain stdout from SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks is injected the same way, as a system reminder starting with the hook's name.

SessionStart additionalContext is added at the start of the conversation, before the first prompt; SessionStart also accepts initialUserMessage (creates the first user turn in -p mode), watchPaths, sessionTitle and reloadSkills.
When several hooks return additionalContext for one event, Claude receives every value.

Cap: additionalContext, systemMessage, initialUserMessage and plain stdout are each capped at 10,000 characters, measured per string. Over the cap, Claude Code saves the text to a file in the session directory and passes the file path plus a preview of up to 2,000 characters. The cap has no setting or environment variable.
Claude Code does not tell Claude to read the saved file.
Several hooks each under 10,000 characters can together exceed it, since each string is measured on its own; a local model can still receive tens of thousands of tokens from hooks. [inferred]
Shell profile output on stdout breaks JSON parsing and the hook JSON has no effect.
A Setup hook's JSON output, including additionalContext, is discarded on every exit code.
UserPromptSubmit hooks default to a 30 second timeout and block model processing until they finish.
Whether the 10,000-character cap applies to hook text injected through the memory-central style per-prompt hooks used here; the size per prompt is not measured.
